standard.title: Generate and develop ideas
standard.description: generate, document and develop ideas for artworks
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can generate and document ideas for artworks using planning strategies (AC9AVA6C01). They have not yet developed sustained visual inquiry, moved through multiple development stages, or justified compositional decisions in relation to intended meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students generate, document and develop ideas for artworks through sustained visual inquiry, making and justifying compositional decisions that connect to intended meaning.

nodes.label: Generating ideas through visual brainstorming
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can generate ideas for artworks through visual brainstorming that explores multiple approaches before committing to a direction
nodes.minimum_width: Complete at least two planning stages for an artwork (e.g. visual brainstorm, compositional sketch); explain what each stage contributed to the developing idea
nodes.typical_width: Generate ideas through sustained visual brainstorming across a range of approaches (images, forms, processes, materials); annotate the process using visual arts terminology; explain which directions were pursued and which were set aside and why
wider: Use Viewpoints to generate questions that push brainstorming beyond familiar territory — document how generative questions open unexpected directions
Explore how combining materials or processes that don't obviously belong together produces surprising possibilities — document the combinations and evaluate which are worth developing
Research how artists use visual brainstorming differently across traditions (e.g. studio sketchbooks, mood boards, material exploration) and experiment with unfamiliar approaches

response_modes.reason: Productive visual brainstorming — staying open, exploring multiple directions, resisting premature commitment — is a studio practice habit developed through sustained repetition. Students who brainstorm once and move to execution haven't built the generative patience that makes ideation genuinely productive. The skill develops through disciplined practice, not through broader contexts.

success_criteria: Completes at least two planning stages
Explains what each stage contributed to the developing idea
Shows evidence of exploring multiple directions before committing

nodes.label: Developing ideas through research and investigation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop ideas through investigation of subject matter, artists and contexts, using research to deepen and refine the artistic concept
nodes.minimum_width: Research at least one source relevant to the artwork idea (an artist, a context, a subject matter angle); explain how the research changed or deepened the idea
nodes.typical_width: Research subject matter, artists and contexts to develop the artwork idea; document how research opens up the concept; make decisions about which directions to pursue based on research findings
wider: Develop an idea through research into subject matter from multiple perspectives — document how shifting perspective changes what the artwork might communicate

Investigate how artists from different cultural contexts have approached the same subject — use findings to develop a distinctively personal approach that is informed by but not derivative of those artists
Explore ideas about significant subjects or concepts through a particular perspective or range of perspectives — document how perspective shifts the artistic problem

response_modes.reason: Students commonly use research to confirm an already-formed idea rather than to genuinely develop it. Investigating subject matter from multiple perspectives, and artists from multiple cultural contexts, forces students to let research change the idea rather than just illustrate it. Multiple research contexts are what builds this as a genuine practice rather than a box-ticking step.

success_criteria: Researches at least one relevant source
Explains how the research changed or deepened the idea — not just describes what was found
Documentation shows research as a generative step, not just background information

nodes.label: Making and justifying compositional decisions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a series of compositional decisions for an artwork and justify each in relation to intended meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least one compositional sketch that documents how visual conventions will communicate the intended meaning; justify at least two specific compositional choices
nodes.typical_width: Develop a series of compositional sketches as planning for a final artwork; make and justify decisions about visual conventions and planned processes; document decisions using visual arts terminology
wider: Develop multiple alternative compositional approaches to the same idea and evaluate each against the intended meaning — document why the chosen approach is strongest
Use Viewpoints questions ('What combinations are surprising?', 'What would happen if I...?', 'How can I push these ideas further?') to generate compositional decisions that go beyond the obvious
Evaluate how other artists' compositional decisions communicate their intended meaning — use the analysis to sharpen own compositional justifications

response_modes.reason: Students commonly make compositional decisions intuitively without being able to articulate a justification connected to intended meaning. Scaffolding the reasoning (what is this composition trying to communicate, what convention serves that purpose, why this rather than the alternative?) builds the reflective practice that makes planning documents genuinely useful rather than perfunctory.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The Viewpoints-driven compositional exploration direction is rich for advancing students — it introduces a structured questioning method that can generate genuinely unexpected directions rather than executing a pre-formed plan. Students who engage this direction develop compositional thinking as an investigative practice.
success_criteria: Develops at least one compositional sketch that documents visual convention choices
Justifies at least two specific compositional choices in relation to intended meaning
Justification goes beyond 'I liked it' — uses visual arts reasoning
